''[[A Different World]]'' }} '''''A Different World''''' is an American [[television comedy|comedy]] television series and a [[Revival (television)|revival]] of the 1987–1993 [[NBC]] [[A Different World|sitcom of the same title]]. The series stars [[Maleah Joi Moon]], with [[Jasmine Guy]] and [[Kadeem Hardison]] reprising their roles from the original series billed as "special guest stars" alongside many other returning actors. It premiered on [[Netflix]] on September 24, 2026, exactly 39 years from the original series premiere date.{{cite web |last1=Maglio |first1=Tony |title=Netflix’s ‘A Different World’ to Premiere 39 Years (to the Day) After the Original Series |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/netflixs-a-different-world-sequel-reboot-premiere-date-1236608537/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=August 12, 2026 |date=May 29, 2026}} It received generally positive reviews from critics. In October 2026, the series was renewed for a second season. ==Premise== When Dwayne Wayne and Whitley Gilbert's free-spirited and kindhearted, yet rebellious youngest child Deborah enters her freshman year at Hillman College, she finds her parents' shadow difficult to escape as she aims to build her own legacy. She does that while also having the time of her life with the new generation of Hillman's finest and brightest.{{cite web |last1=Romero |first1=Ariana |last2=Bentley |first2=Jean |title=A Different World Will Take You Back to Hillman College This September |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/a-different-world-sequel-series-hillman-college |website=Tudum |publisher=Netflix |access-date=August 12, 2026 |date=July 20, 2026 |archive-date=March 25, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260325224942/https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/a-different-world-sequel-series-hillman-college |url-status=live}} ==Cast and characters== {{Main|List of A Different World characters}} ===Main=== *[[Maleah Joi Moon]] as Deborah Wayne *Alijah Kai as Rashida Duvall *Cornell Young IV as Shaquille Johnson *Jordan Aaron Hall as Amir Rodale *Kennedi Reece as Hazel Henry *[[Chibuikem Uche]] as Kojo Achebe ===Special guest=== *[[Jasmine Guy]] as [[Whitley Gilbert-Wayne]] *[[Kadeem Hardison]] as [[Dwayne Wayne]] *[[Darryl M. Bell]] as Ron Johnson *[[Cree Summer]] as Freddie Brooks ===Recurring=== *[[Ajai Sanders]] as Gina Deveaux *[[Karen Malina White]] as Charmaine Brown *[[Charnele Brown]] as Dr. Kimberly Reese Boyer *[[Jenifer Lewis]] as Professor Davenport *[[Dawnn Lewis]] as Jaleesa Vinson-Taylor *[[Glynn Turman]] as Colonel Bradford Taylor *[[Jada Pinkett Smith]] as Congresswoman Lena James *[[Method Man|Cliff "Method Man" Smith]] as Coach Coles *Norman Nixon Jr. as Professor Baptiste *Vincent Jamal Hooper as Ellington Kendall *[[Elijah J. Roberts]] as Jalen *Renee Harrison as Candace *Famecia Ward as Nellie Gaines *Dasan Frazier as Xavier *[[Tichina Arnold]] as Darlene Duvall *Joshua Suiter as Andre *[[Raven Goodwin]] as Dr. Brooklyn Boyer *Imani Guy Duckette as Teedra ==Episodes== {{Episode table |background=#000000 |overall= |title= |director= |writer= |airdate= |episodes= {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 1 |Title = Irreconcilable Differences |DirectedBy = [[Debbie Allen]] |WrittenBy = [[Felicia Pride]] |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = Deborah Wayne, the youngest daughter of Dwayne Wayne and Whitley Gilbert-Wayne, begins her freshman year at Hillman College, following in her parents' footsteps. She moves in with her new roommate and begins meeting the students who will become her core group of friends. Her attempt at starting fresh is complicated when she discovers that Shaquille, an old boyfriend, is also at Hillman. Deborah also quickly learns that being Dwayne and Whitley's daughter means people already have expectations of her before she's had a chance to establish herself. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 2 |Title = O Captain! My Captain! |DirectedBy = Tiffany Johnson |WrittenBy = Des Moran |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = Deborah gets herself into trouble after openly expressing her opinion and finds herself being called out publicly on campus. Rashida, struggling financially, looks for ways to make extra money while keeping up with college. Meanwhile, Shaquille prepares for his first Hillman football game, but the game doesn't go the way he expected. The episode starts showing the different pressures facing the group: Deborah's reputation, Rashida's finances and Shaquille's athletic expectations. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 3 |Title = Center de Stage |DirectedBy = Angela Barnes |WrittenBy = Lisa McQuillan |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = It's Homecoming weekend, bringing a number of Hillman alumni back to campus. Deborah becomes caught up in trying to secure a headlining performer for the Homecoming festivities. Dwayne and Whitley return to Hillman, but it becomes increasingly obvious that there are serious tensions in their marriage. Their problems begin affecting Deborah at the same time she's trying to manage her own increasingly complicated college life. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 4 |Title = Those Who Can...Cuff |DirectedBy = Angela Barnes |WrittenBy = Howard Jordan Jr. |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = “Cuffing season” arrives at Hillman and the students' romantic relationships start becoming considerably messier. Dates and hookups intersect with academic pressure and financial problems. Deborah's romantic situation becomes increasingly complicated, while the relationships among the rest of the friend group begin shifting as well. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 5 |Title = Final Words |DirectedBy = Tiffany Johnson |WrittenBy = [[Rashida Olayiwola]] |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = Final exams begin and Deborah and the entire group are overwhelmed by academic pressure. Different members of the group struggle with the expectations being placed on them and the possibility that they won't perform as well as they hoped. A more serious crisis then interrupts the finals panic and forces everyone to reconsider what they're worrying about and what actually matters. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 6 |Title = Insomnia and the Daydreamer |DirectedBy = Tiffany Johnson |WrittenBy = Des Moran & Ashley Laverne Jackson |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = Deborah starts questioning whether the man she's been imagining as her ideal partner is actually right for her. Her unresolved feelings and romantic options become increasingly difficult to ignore. Meanwhile, the students go out for a night at a club, only for the evening to become chaotic when the aunties unexpectedly arrive. The resulting night mixes the younger characters' romantic drama with interference from the older generation. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 7 |Title = Sometimes You Get the Culture...Sometimes the Culture Gets You |DirectedBy = [[Nefertite Nguvu]] |WrittenBy = Howard Jordan Jr., Tasha Armstead, Joel Armstead |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = Hillman holds its end-of-year talent show, where Deborah and Kojo set out to prove people who doubted them wrong. Kojo also finds himself caught up in arguments surrounding African/diaspora identity and culture. Hazel competes for Miss Gilbert Hall, giving her a chance to establish herself on campus. At the same time, the students deal with issues surrounding sexual health and relationships. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 8 |Title = I Choose Chaos |DirectedBy = Nefertite Nguvu |WrittenBy = Felicia Pride & Des Moran |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = A tornado warning traps the students inside, meaning several people who have been avoiding difficult conversations can no longer get away from each other. Hazel and Amir are forced to confront their ongoing conflict. Deborah and Shaquille finally discuss their original breakup, revealing more about what went wrong between them before Hillman. Their conversation also makes it increasingly difficult for Deborah to pretend that her feelings for Shaquille are entirely in the past. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 9 |Title = Romancing the Unknown |DirectedBy = [[Bille Woodruff]] |WrittenBy = Lisa McQuillan |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = The situation at Hillman becomes much more serious when the college's budget crisis erupts. Deborah and her friends decide they aren't simply going to sit back and watch what happens and begin taking action themselves. At the same time, the long-running problems between Dwayne and Whitley come to a head, putting Deborah in the middle of a major family conflict while she's also becoming involved in the fight over Hillman's future. |LineColor = 000000 }} {{Episode list |EpisodeNumber = 10 |Title = A Gift & The Curse |DirectedBy = Bille Woodruff |WrittenBy = Felicia Pride |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|9|24}} |ShortSummary = The end-of-year gala brings the various storylines together as Hillman's financial problems, the students' relationships and Deborah's family situation reach their respective breaking points. The students' response to the Hillman crisis puts Deborah in an increasingly active role in campus affairs, while major decisions are made about the college's future. Relationships that have developed throughout the year are forced to either move forward or fall apart, and Deborah faces a major decision in her own love life. The finale also establishes a new chapter for Hillman and leaves several characters facing very different futures going into their next year. |LineColor = 000000 }} }} ==Production== === Development === On August 23 and 24, 2012, [[Debbie Allen]] wrote on [[Twitter]] that she wanted to reboot the series. Over a million people on [[Facebook]], Twitter, and blogs reacted to the tweet and approved of the potential reboot.{{cite web |last=Witherspoon |first=Chris |date=August 24, 2012 |title=Debbie Allen wants to bring 'A Different World' back to TV |url=https://thegrio.com/2012/08/24/debbie-allen-wants-to-bring-a-different-world-back-to-tv/ |website=[[TheGrio]] |location=United States |publisher=[[Allen Media Group]] |access-date=August 12, 2026}}{{cite web |last= |first= |date=August 27, 2012 |title=Director Debbie Allen Wants “A Different World” Back On Air |url=https://www.vibe.com/news/movies-tv/director-debbie-allen-wants-different-world-back-air-108826/ |work=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]] |location=United States |publisher=[[Eldridge Industries]] |access-date=August 12, 2026}} On August 7, 2024, [[Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']] reported that a sequel to the series was in the works at [[Netflix]]: a [[Single-camera setup|single-camera]] half-hour comedy focusing on original cast characters Whitley & Dwayne's daughter, who also attends Hillman College. ''Deadline'' indicated that the series would be written and produced by [[Felicia Pride]], who has worked on ''[[Bel-Air (TV series)|Bel-Air]]'' and ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'', and that Debbie Allen would be an executive producer, along with Mandy Summers, [[Tom Werner]], [[Gina Prince-Bythewood]] and [[Reggie Rock Bythewood|Reggie Bythewood]].{{cite web |last=Cordero |first=Rosy premiered on [[Netflix]] on September 24, 2026. == Reception == The review aggregator website [[Rotten Tomatoes]] reported a 82% approval rating based on 22 critic reviews. The website's critics consensus reads, "This revived continuation of a beloved classic follows new characters through the lens of Gen-Z, crackling with energy, strutting with style, and written with full-hearted verve, proving that ''A Different World'' isn't such a bad thing after all."{{Cite web |title=A Different World: Season 1 {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/a_different_world_2026/s01 |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.rottentomatoes.com |language=en |archive-date=September 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260923085550/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/a_different_world_2026/s01 |url-status=live}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 72 out of 100, based on 13 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.{{Cite web |title=A Different World (2026) Reviews - Metacritic |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/a-different-world-2026/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.metacritic.com |language=en}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{Official website|https://www.netflix.com/title/81747525}} * {{IMDb title}} {{The Cosby Show}} {{Netflix original current series}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Different World, A}} [[Category:A Different World| ]] [[Category:2026 American television series debuts]] [[Category:2026 English-language television series debuts]] [[Category:2020s American black sitcoms]] [[Category:2020s American college television series]] [[Category:2020s American LGBTQ-related comedy television series]] [[Category:2020s American single-camera sitcoms]] [[Category:2020s American teen sitcoms]] [[Category:American television series about teenagers]] [[Category:American television spinoffs]] [[Category:English-language American television shows]] [[Category:Netflix sitcoms]] [[Category:Television series by Carsey-Werner Productions]] [[Category:Television series created by Bill Cosby]] [[Category:The Cosby Show]]
